chunks: I asked Abū al-Ḥasan عليه السلام about the saying of Allah, Mighty and Majestic:
"And whoever is blind in this [life], he will be blind in the Hereafter and further astray in way."

So he عليه السلام said: "It was revealed about one who delays the hajj, the hajj of Islam, while he has what he can perform hajj with, and says, 'This year I will perform hajj, this year I will perform hajj,' until he dies before performing hajj."

key_terms.أَعْمَىٰ: blind; here, spiritually blind to an obligatory duty
key_terms.الْآخِرَةِ: the Hereafter, where the consequence of such neglect appears
key_terms.حَجَّةَ الْإِسْلَامِ: the obligatory hajj required once in a lifetime

ai.seo_question: What does the verse about being blind in this life and the Hereafter mean in relation to delaying hajj?
ai.summary: This hadith explains the verse as referring to a person who keeps postponing the obligatory hajj despite having the means to perform it. Their blindness is a moral and religious blindness shown through neglect of a clear divine duty until death overtakes them.
